newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria shops for arms in North Korea, China.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria shops for arms in North Korea, China.

text.p: Nigeria's chief of defence staff returned home on Monday from a trip to North Korea and China optimistic that they would provide arms which Western states refuse to sell to his military government.
Lieutenant-General Abdulsalam Abubakar told reporters on his return to the Nigerian capital Abuja that no deals had been signed, but he hoped agreements would soon be reached.
"The negotiations, apart from in the area of armaments, also covered other military assistance we have identified which both countries can offer us," Abubakar said.

Military-ruled Nigeria has been shunned by its former Western allies. They accuse the government of human rights abuses and have expressed scepticism about its stated intention to give up power next year.
Limited sanctions were imposed by many Western states after the 1995 execution of minority rights activist Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight others for murder.
Since then, Nigeria has increasingly turned to Asia and has signed several large civil engineering deals with Chinese contractors.
Africa's most populous nation has been in political turmoil since 1993, when a previous military government annulled elections which would have ended a decade of rule by soldiers.
